content: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer met with French President Emmanuel Macron in Paris on Monday to discuss a new border agreement between the United Kingdom and France. The talks, which lasted nearly three hours, also covered defense cooperation within NATO. Officials from both governments said a joint statement would be released later this week. Starmer told reporters that the meeting was constructive and that both countries were committed to reducing illegal crossings in the English Channel.

The United Nations warned in New York that the humanitarian crisis in Sudan could worsen over the coming months. Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said that millions of people have been displaced since the conflict began, and that aid organizations such as the Red Cross and Doctors Without Borders are struggling to reach affected areas. The World Food Programme has requested an additional two billion dollars to continue its operations in the region. Several countries, including Germany and Japan, have pledged new funding.

The Federal Reserve held interest rates steady on Wednesday after a two-day meeting in Washington. Chair Jerome Powell said the central bank would continue to monitor inflation and employment data before making any changes. Markets on Wall Street reacted calmly, with the S&P 500 closing slightly higher. Analysts at Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan expect the first rate cut to arrive early next year, depending on how the economy performs over the winter.

Lionel Messi scored two goals as Inter Miami defeated Orlando City 3-1 at Chase Stadium in Florida on Saturday night. The Argentine forward opened the scoring in the 12th minute and added a second from the penalty spot after halftime. Coach Javier Mascherano praised the team for its discipline and said the victory moves Inter Miami closer to the top of the Eastern Conference. The club will travel to Atlanta next weekend to face Atlanta United.

Tesla announced that it will open a new factory in Monterrey, Mexico, with an investment of five billion dollars. Chief Executive Elon Musk said the plant is expected to create more than ten thousand jobs and begin production in 2028. Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum welcomed the decision during a press conference in Mexico City and said her government would work with the company on infrastructure and energy supply. The announcement comes as automakers such as Ford and General Motors also expand their operations in the country.
